about: Claim-to-citation support labels. Each claim cites one passage; label = whether that passage supports the claim. Labelled by the developer by reading the fixture text (not an independent reviewer). Includes known-hard cases (negation, wrong number) on purpose.

passages.bio1: The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer that controls which substances enter and leave the cell. Embedded transport proteins move ions such as sodium and potassium across the membrane. Small nonpolar molecules like oxygen diffuse directly through the bilayer.
passages.bio2: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's ATP through cellular respiration. Glucose is first split during glycolysis in the cytoplasm, and the citric acid cycle then runs inside the mitochondrial matrix. Aerobic respiration yields about 38 ATP per glucose molecule in older textbook estimates.
passages.bio3: Chloroplasts capture light energy using chlorophyll pigments. The light-dependent reactions in the thylakoid membranes split water and release oxygen. The Calvin cycle in the stroma fixes carbon dioxide into sugar using ATP and NADPH.
passages.bio4: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells and has four phases: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. During metaphase the chromosomes line up along the cell's equator. Meiosis instead produces four genetically different gametes with half the chromosome number.
passages.bio5: Enzymes are proteins that speed up reactions by lowering the activation energy. Each enzyme has an active site that binds a specific substrate. High temperatures can denature an enzyme so that its active site no longer fits the substrate.
passages.errata: Correction to the mitochondria page: current estimates put aerobic respiration at about 30 to 32 ATP per glucose molecule, not 38, because transporting molecules into the mitochondria costs energy. Correction to the revision checklist: the unit test moved from Friday to Monday.
passages.stats2: A residual equals observed Y minus predicted Y_hat. Ordinary least squares fits beta_0 and beta_1 by minimizing the sum of squared residuals. Large residuals suggest poor fit for a particular observation.
passages.stats3: A basic linear regression analysis assumes a linear mean relationship and makes assumptions about residual behavior. Correlation does not prove causation. Extrapolating far outside the observed X range is risky.
